searchText: I think I'm misunderstanding `RESERVE_GAS`. If I have 10000 AA contracts that all do a `STATICCALL` into some contract `0xbaadf00d...` and read a variable (prior to `PAYGAS`), someone can set that variable such that all 10000 of those AA contracts are invalidated with a single external call. How would you determine how much `RESERVE_GAS` is needed (in this case, we need to ensure it is 10,000 * minimum)? `RESERVE_GAS` is for the other way around, when a non-AA transaction writes into an AA contract. <@!301186049323958275> I updated the wording to make that more clear; thanks! <@!689161464829050960> With AA contracts able to do `STATIC_CALL` prior to `PAYGAS` though, you don't have to touch the AA contract in order to invalidate it. AA contracts would still only be able to `DELEGATECALL` out. The changes here only permit static/limited non-static calls _into_ AA contracts. I am wondering how an ability to write to the state of target account in verification part of Tx can be used? Oh, so there is still no plan for allowing AA contracts to call out? Not before `PAYGAS`, no > I am wondering how an ability to write to the state of target account in verification part of Tx can be used? <@!425572898787426305> Like an example use case? If your AA contract maintains a balance for each user, you could deduct gas price * gas limit before PAYGAS. You mean a fee for the verification part? oh, I see now, just a regular fee and do a refund at the end Yep! that makes a lot of sense to me now, thx I think that my problem with AA may be that I keep thinking about it from the standpoint of being able to do a bunch of interesting stuff before PAYGAS. Really, I should be thinking about them just as normal contract with likely a single owner where the contract can pay for gas. I think that leaves me in a place where the only real change I would like to see is some kind of support for sponsored transactions. I don't think it's fair to say you can't do a bunch of interesting stuff before `PAYGAS`. Using zk proofs, multisig schemes, and all that are certainly interesting :P All the restrictions are to ensure that once a transaction is valid, the only thing that can invalidate it is another transaction to the same contract. All of the things I think I have in my head for AA are really things that should happen *after* PAYGAS. The only requirement *prior* to PAYGAS is verifying that the transaction is valid *enough* to have the contract deduct gas fees. And in most cases that just means checking "is this data signed by a valid signer", which is unlikely to need to be looked up externally. https://twitter.com/owocki/status/1316380501347762177 spliced up the videos from yesterday into bite sized chunks for yall 🙂 Recording of the Ethereum Engineering Group session on account abstraction: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_DUHTJEoaX0

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: I think I'm misunderstanding `RESERVE_GAS`.  If I have 10000 AA contracts that all do a `STATICCALL` into some contract `0xbaadf00d...` and read a variable (prior to `PAYGAS`), someone can set that variable such that all 10000 of those AA contracts are invalidated with a single external call.  How would you determine how much `RESERVE_GAS` is needed (in this case, we need to ensure it is 10,000 * minimum)?

excerpts.author: samwilsn
excerpts.content: `RESERVE_GAS` is for the other way around, when a non-AA transaction writes into an AA contract.

excerpts.author: samwilsn
excerpts.content: <@!301186049323958275> I updated the wording to make that more clear; thanks!

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: <@!689161464829050960> With AA contracts able to do `STATIC_CALL` prior to `PAYGAS` though, you don't have to touch the AA contract in order to invalidate it.

excerpts.author: samwilsn
excerpts.content: AA contracts would still only be able to `DELEGATECALL` out. The changes here only permit static/limited non-static calls _into_ AA contracts.
